title: Dedicated autoscaler: priority burst utilization reporting enhancement + SLO fallback
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: Dedicated fleet customers have seen noisy burst utilization metrics when priority routing and token-bucket smoothing are enabled which made SLO fallbacks trigger too aggressively. This PR improves utilization accounting for priority lanes, adds per-priority rolling windows for burst reporting, and introduces an optional SLO fallback policy that gracefully throttles low-priority traffic when capacity is constrained. Motivation: reduce false-positive SLO regressions, give operators actionable per-priority utilization metrics, and provide a safe fallback so customer-facing high-priority traffic maintains latency. Changes: 1) compute per-priority token consumption and expose new metrics: dedicated.autoscaler.priority_utilization and dedicated.autoscaler.burst_headroom_{priority}. 2) replace single-window util calc with configurable rolling windows (config defaults to [1m,5m,15m]) and apply exponential smoothing to reduce spikes from short-lived bursts. 3) wire SLO fallback policy into routing layer: when aggregate effective_utilization > configured_slo_threshold, low-priority lanes get an automated degrade policy (queue-length caps + reduced token refill) with an immediate alert. 4) update telemetry docs and add internal dashboard panels and unit/integration tests. Rollout: feature flag `autoscaler.priority_burst_reporting_v2` gated for dedicated accounts; default off for existing fleets. Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-1123) - [x] unit tests - [x] integration test with local dedicated simulator - [x] metrics and dashboards updated - [x] backward-compatible default config - [x] staged rollout plan and feature flag - [x] updated release notes for operators Backwards compatibility: metrics names are additive; old endpoints still provide legacy util but a migration guide is included.
